title: The Ledger
logline: A village shop's handwritten credit book holds decades of small debts, some paid next week, some after the harvest, some quietly struck through when the debtor dies.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: What a community gives one of its own becomes what is owed on paper: a village shop's credit book, where some debts are struck through when the debtor dies.

thread_out.thread: The question of whether everything owed comes due moves from a ledger to a paddy field, where the rain that should keep coming simply stops.

requirements: A working village shop with a handwritten credit system and a shopkeeper willing to be filmed
Customers willing to be filmed at the counter, or filming arranged to protect their privacy

suggestions.name: A tea-estate village shop in the Nuwara Eliya or Uda Pussellawa area
suggestions.why: Small rural shops with long-running credit books are still common in tea-growing hill country.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts teach that what we do does not all come due at the same time: some of it shows up in this life, some in the next, some waits a very long time for an opening, and some simply lapses and never comes due at all.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අප කරන දේවල ඵල එකවර නොලැබෙන බවත්, සමහරක් මේ ජීවිතයේම, සමහරක් ඊළඟ ජීවිතයේ, සමහරක් අවස්ථාවක් එනතුරු දිගු කලක් රැඳී සිට ලැබෙන බවත්, සමහරක් කිසිදා ඵල නොදී අහෝසි වී යන බවත් ග්‍රන්ථ කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Under the time of ripening, the Abhidhamma sorts intentional action into four kinds: to be experienced in this life, in the next life, in some later life whenever there is an opening, and lapsed action that never ripens. Action lapses when it misses its window or when a stronger action takes its place, like seed grain kept past its season. The Margaya adds that ordinary acts may ripen in this very life without the person even noticing.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Across a season at the counter, some accounts are settled next week, some after the harvest, and some are quietly struck through when the debtor dies. The shopkeeper's memory and the worn pages let the viewer feel how debts keep different clocks, and one line crossed out for good carries, without a word of doctrine, the image of something whose moment simply passed.

key_terms.en: fourfold division of action by time of ripening
opening or opportunity for a result to ripen
lapsed or defunct action; action that never ripens

lesson.caution: A credit book is only a picture: kamma is not a ledger that balances, lapsed action is not forgiveness, and this is not 'what goes around comes around'.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed a community holding one of its own through a night; this one turns to what is owed between people, and adds that results keep different clocks and some never come due.
